MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETINGS OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
May 6, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on Monday, May
6, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Traina led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to the roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
City Attorney Hogin, Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation Director Harding,
Administrative Services Director Chavez, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

3. SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Estrada and Councilmembers presented a certificate of recognition to Patricia Kromka for
receiving one of the Women of Distinction Awards for District 66 of the California State
Assembly.

4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock reported that he had a meeting with Maurice Lyles, Field Representative for
U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer, during which local-level issues were discussed.

City Manager Rock also reported that the Cypress Water Production Facility is operating well
with the current blend ratio of 75/25, and that only one complaint had been received within the
past week regarding water quality. City Manager Rock added that both methane and TDS levels
remain the same.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Gazeley reported that he attended the Southern California Association of

  Page 1
 Governments (SCAG) Regional Conference and that one of the sessions he participated in was
on the economic recovery in Southern California, where the elimination of state tax was
discussed as the possible remedy to retain businesses in California.

Councilmember Gazeley also reported that at the last South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCG) he met with the Representative of the California League of Cities, who provided
Councilmember Gazeley with a list of proposed bills. According to Councilmember Gazeley, the
City needs to pay close attention to proposed bills AB 5 and AB 162, as they could affect the
City if passed, by requiring the City to provide social services to people with mental disabilities
(AB 5), and changing the requirements for telecommunication facilities (AB 162).
Councilmember Gazeley added that the City Council needs to be more proactive, and in turn
communicate issues with proposed bills early to State Representatives, before the bills are
passed.

Councilmember Sanchez reported that 23 volunteers completed the latest CERT class in
Lomita. Councilmember Sanchez also invited those in attendance to the Lomita Fire Fighters
Spaghetti Dinner, which will be held on Friday, May 10, 2013, from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m., at the
Kiwanis Club.

Councilmember Traina requested two future agenda items: consideration of establishing a policy
for texting and the use of electronic devices at City Council meetings, and discussion on
whether stating one’s name and address for the record during public meetings is a necessary
requirement. Discussion followed as to whether electronic devices, such as iPads, could be
used to display the agenda packet during Council meetings. City Attorney Hogin stated that
there is an upcoming training scheduled for June 5, 2013, and that the two agenda items
requested by Councilmember Traina will be covered in the training curriculum.

Councilmember Traina also stated that he had received one anonymous complaint regarding a
water heater issue, which the resident claimed was related to water hardness issues. According
to Councilmember Traina, well water is degrading the quality of Metropolitan water, and that for
blended water to be economically viable, the blend should be 50/50. Councilmember Traina
added that residents, as well as water ratepayers, have the right to request good water, and that
he opposes the use of well water.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, stated that the water hardness target numbers were established
without any explanation to the public about what those numbers mean. According to Mr.
McGrath, the City’s target numbers for water hardness are too high; Mr. McGrath went on to
provide some information he obtained via research regarding the hardness of water, and how it
could affect a person’s health. Mr. McGrath urged City Council to stop the water blending until
long-term considerations have been given to protect the health of Lomita residents.

Scott Gobble, Board Member of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, invited those in attendance
to the 9th Annual Golden Apple Awards Dinner, which will be held on Thursday, May 9, 2013,
from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. Mr. Gobble also announced that the next Business Networking Mixer will
take place at the South Bay Health and Wellness Center on May 23, 2013, from 5:30 p.m. to
7:30 p.m., and that the Business Networking Mixer scheduled for June 27, 2013, will take place
at the Summer Studios Arts Academy.

  Page 2
 Sharon Houston, Lomita resident, agreed with Councilmember Traina that the City needs a
texting policy. Ms. Houston also stated that the tap water in her house has a strong chlorine
smell.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, stated that the City Council needs to consider residents’ health,
and in turn provide quality water to its residents. Mr. Friedrich also asked why staff did not
inform Council and the public that the Lomita bonds had been downgraded to an “A” rating,
which Mr. Friedrich stated he discovered through an online article.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Mayor Estrada pulled Item 7.B from the Consent Agenda for discussion, Councilmember
Gazeley pulled Item 7.L, and Councilmember Traina pulled Item 7.G.

Item 7.B - Mayor Estrada stated that for the record she would like to add a statement into the
minutes that Ken Blackwood on behalf of the Lion’s Club donated $300 for the Arbor Day event.

Item 7.G - Councilmember Traina asked whether the 16-unit condominiums were allowable
under the current zoning, to which City Manager Rock responded affirmatively that they meet
current zoning requirements.

Item 7.L - Councilmember Gazeley clarified that the letter regarding the possible consolidation of
the Lomita Business Mail Entry with the Torrance Business Mail Entry only moves 33 business
mail entry units (bulk mail) to the Torrance Post Office. Councilmember Gazeley added that this
does not mean that the Lomita Post Office is closing.

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the Consent Agenda.  Councilmember Savidan
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for a Special and Regular City Council Meeting
  held on April 15, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  d. Monthly Report for the Community Development Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  f. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Monthly Report regarding Economic Development Activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. March 2013 Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  j. Approval of Final Tract Map 53874. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  Page 3
   k. Consideration of a Resolution of Intention and Preparation of the Engineer’s Report for
  Landscape Maintenance District No.1. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  l. Authorization to sign a letter regarding the possible consolidation of the Lomita Post Office
  Business Mail Entry Unit (BMEU) to the Torrance Post Office. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

8.  BUDGET WORKSHOP AND PUBLIC HEARING SCHEDULE

  Councilmembers agreed to schedule a budget workshop for Wednesday, May 22, 2013 at 6
  p.m., and to have consideration of the adoption of the 2013-2014 Fiscal Year Budget be
  scheduled for Monday, June 3, 2013.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:35 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

_________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
